note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the changes named. RFC 9234 Section 5: "The OTC Attribute is considered malformed if the length value is not 4. An UPDATE message with a malformed OTC Attribute SHALL be handled using the approach of "treat-as-withdraw" [RFC7606]." The earlier weak finding (no tagged unit proved the handling, only the withdraw verdict) is answered by the new tag on test/plugin/role-otc-malformed-treat-as-withdraw.ci (b5990018f7): ze with bgp-role, a Provider source and a Customer dest. Negative: the source's 10.0.0.0/24 with OTC C0 23 04 0000FDE9 must reach the dest as an announcement still carrying that OTC (dest seq 1). Positive: the same prefix re-sent with OTC length 3 must reach the dest as exactly the withdrawal FF..001B020004180A00000000 (dest seq 2) with no attributes, so the earlier announcement is removed on the wire, the RFC 7606 treat-as-withdraw outcome; a reject would leave seq 2 absent, an accept would send an announcement. Isolation: the source is a Provider, so no leak rule rejects either UPDATE, and a length-3 OTC read as absent would be stamped and announced, so only the malformed rule yields the withdrawal; a barrier route makes the dest an established target first. Discrimination: otc.go checkOTCIngress isMalformed disabled reddens the positive, findOTC length check forced true reddens the negative (judged genuine by ze-test-judge this session). Lengths 0, 5 and 8 are proven at the decision level by the byte-identical Go units. Whole requirement now covered: decision and handling. Verdict: enforced (was weak).
